method: Addressed educational-admission interpretation of saved endpoint review; no new collision scan or transformation
interpretation: All21 components per side have a craniomedial geometric course. This supports one broad directional feature, not confirmed origin/insertion.

Nearest-source-bone cap matches suggest11 single-level and10 two-level bundles per side. These are candidate labels, not attachment mapping; continuous surface and named bone subparts were not segmented.
C7 is in the source endpoint search but absent from the atlas comparison subset. Distances around10–11mm from these caps to T1 must NOT be reported as proven attachment gaps.

Authors label the object multifidus thoracis and their bundled description includes deepest adjacent-vertebra slips. Modern sources often separate multifidus and rotatores by span/depth. No relabelling to rotatores or arbitrary component deletion is justified by nearest-bone span alone.
Contacts in a geometric middle bin need anatomical subpart review. A height fraction or material name does not establish an attachment or a major defect.

Educational admission is withheld for unresolved specimen-specific muscle identity/major endpoint relationships and parent compatibility, NOT for absence of precise surgical margins. Counts of crossings alone were not used as rejection criteria.
